key_insight: A 3D CNN can learn subgrid turbulent transport in quiet-Sun simulations by using velocity and density fields to better reconstruct Reynolds stress tensor components than simpler ML or classic turbulence models.
engineering_relevance: This offers a data-driven surrogate for unresolved solar plasma turbulence, which could improve coarse-grid radiative hydrodynamic simulations of the solar convection zone and lower atmosphere.
method: Train a 3D convolutional neural network on 3D velocity fields plus scalar plasma density features.
Predict Reynolds stress tensor components and test activation/architecture variants, including a log transform of skewed targets.
Benchmark against an MLP and physics-based Gradient and Smagorinsky models.
evidence_signal: The final 3DCNN improved reconstruction by about 31% on diagonal stress components and about 8% on off-diagonal components relative to comparison baselines.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the specific quiet-Sun simulation regime and careful handling of strongly skewed target distributions during training and deployment.
paper_title: Developing Machine Learning Models of Subgrid Turbulent Transport for Quiet Sun 3D Radiative Hydrodynamic Simulations
